title: Broomstick lace cowl
excerpt: A quick loop cowl in DK yarn using broomstick lace clusters. Worked flat and seamed, it sits comfortably around the neck with a soft drape.
sourceNotes: A short flat panel in broomstick lace, seamed at the short ends to form a cowl loop. Working in DK keeps the clusters bold and the project quick.

glossaryTerms.definition: In broomstick lace, the row where all loops have been placed on the dowel and are slipped off in groups to form clusters with double crochets.
The join that closes a flat crochet panel into a loop. Usually worked by holding the cast-on and bind-off ends together and slip-stitching or whip-stitching through both layers.

crochet.gaugeText: 3 clusters (15 sts) x 5 rows = 10 cm in broomstick lace on 4.0 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 60 cm circumference x 25 cm deep.

content.text: This cowl uses a short flat panel in broomstick lace, then closes it with a
slides clusters of 5 off the dowel each time.
Chain 50. Row 1: dc in 2nd ch from hook and each ch to end (50 dc). Do not turn.

Loop row: draw up a loop from every stitch onto the dowel (50 loops). Return row: slide 5 loops off the dowel onto the hook, ch 1, work 5 dc through the centre of those 5 loops. Repeat across (10 clusters). Repeat loop and return rows until the panel measures 60 cm.
Fasten off. Fold the panel so the cast-on and last row align. Use the tapestry needle to whip-stitch the short edges together. Weave in all ends.
